newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER STABLE, INTEREST THIN.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER STABLE, INTEREST THIN.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were mostly stable in late trading on Friday on light buying interest from Singapore dealers, traders said.
They said the Singapore players bought September shipment rubber at 42.75 cents fob Palembang, and October shipments at 43.25 cents. September offers of 43.25 cents got no takers.
The traders also said that rumours in Singapore that the Thai government would soon sell its stocks of some 74,000 tonnes had yet to seep into the Indonesian market.
"I have not heard of it," one trader said. "But if it happens, prices will be in for a beating."
A Thai industry official told rubber producers and buyers on the tourist island of Bali last weekend that Thailand had 140,000 tonnes of stocks, half of it with the government.
An advisor to the Thai agriculture ministry, however, said on Wednesday the government would not sell its stocks any time soon.
Another trader said he was sceptical that the Thai government had such a large amount of stocks, but added that any large-scale selling would drive down prices.
"The market is quite fragile at the moment, and any negative news will hit us hard," he added.
Traders said that October SIR20 was offered at 43.50 cents fob Medan, 43.00-43.25 cents fob Palembang, Padang and Surabaya.
